title: MTU oddity and install shim — weekly journal (Mar 05 2026)
content:
Summary:
This is a working-week journal capturing the MTU-related network flapping we saw across two on‑prem installs (HelixAI and Pylon Health), the temporary install shim we rolled to unblock customer installs, and the next steps for durable fixes. Intended as a single‑place update for install engineers, SRE, and solutions.

Context / why this matters:
- Two installs in the last 10 days saw tokenization stalls and intermittent request timeouts that traced back to sporadic TCP retransmits, large packet drops, and asymmetric PMTU discovery failures.
- Both customers are using private interconnects (partner MPLS/VXLAN overlay) with BGP/ECMP on the customer edge. The symptom set looked like application-level latency spikes (200–600ms p95) with occasional full request failures during steady state.

Timeline (concise):
- 2026-02-24 09:40 PST: HelixAI first reported repeated backend stalls during long chat sessions.
- 2026-02-25 14:10 PST: Initial field triage — suspected kernel offload + jumbo-MTU misconfig between ToR and customer firewall.
- 2026-02-26 03:20 UTC: Pylon Health reported nearly identical stalls after an OS patch on their edge router.
- 2026-02-27 11:00 UTC: SRE and Solutions replicated packet drops in lab with MTU mismatch + PMTU blackhole test vectors.
- 2026-03-01 02:00 PST: Deployed temporary 'install shim' (TCP MSS clamp + UDP traceroute probe) to both customers; immediate reduction of application failures.
- 2026-03-03 16:30 PST: Weekly installs sync. Decided to replace shim with per-site kernel config guidance + long‑term fix plan.

Observed impact and frequency:
- HelixAI: ~10–15% requests affected during peak; p95 latency regressed 200–500ms; 3 full request failures/day.
- Pylon Health: ~5% requests affected; p95 latency +120–300ms; 1–2 failures/day.
- Business risk: HelixAI is in extended pilot with high SLA expectations next quarter.

Debug steps taken so far (lab + field):
- Collected tcpdump captures on both endpoints and core switch mirrors (see attached traces).
- Reproduced PMTU blackhole locally by simulating intermediary MTU=1400 path with ICMP rate-limited.
- Verified that Linux kernel path MTU discovery sometimes suppressed ICMP unreachable due to firewall rules; resulted in silent packet drops for large SYN+payload segments.
- Tested kernel tunables (net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1/2) — mitigates but not fully reliable with certain middlebox behaviors.
- Implemented TCP MSS clamp at port 443 on the nginx sidecar as a shim; validated with synthetic load.

Temporary mitigation (install shim) details:
- What we rolled: iptables-based MSS clamping and a small traceroute-based health probe that runs every 30s and flips a local flag if PMTU is suspect.
- Rationale: minimal surface area change to customer stacks; quick rollback; no kernel recompiles.
- Observed benefit: immediate drop in request failures, p95 nearly returned to baseline in canary sessions.
- Risks: the shim is a band-aid — it masks the customer network misconfiguration; if left indefinitely it may hide regressions that need to be surfaced for the customer's networking team.

Hypotheses for root cause (prioritized):
1) MTU mismatch between customer edge and intermediate device + ICMP blackholing by firewall (most likely).
2) ECMP path asymmetry causing large packets to traverse a path that drops fragments while smaller packets take different path.
3) Kernel offload interaction on customer NICs (LSO/GSO) leading to reassembly issues seen as retransmits.

Decisions made in meeting (2026-03-03 installs sync):
- Keep shim active for both customers for up to 14 days while long-term fixes progress.
- Solutions to coordinate a customer-side network change window (bring MTU/gso offload settings in alignment).
- SRE to propose a passive-detection enhancement: surfacing PMTU failures in the install telemetry (new metric + alert).

Action items (owner — ETA):
- Evan Brooks: Draft per-customer network checklist with explicit MTU/GSO/GRO validation steps and sign-off template — due 2026-03-10.
- Lucas Martinez: Add PMTU-detect telemetry to install agent and create dashboard tile + PagerDuty rule (DEPLOY-421) — due 2026-03-12.
- Sophie Patel: Coordinate HelixAI network change window and validate post-change with full load test — target week of 2026-03-15.
- Diego Alvarez: Run kernel offload regression suite against customer NIC firmware versions and report anomalies — due 2026-03-16.
- Priya Narang (me): Draft postmortem-style note and customer-facing summary for HelixAI execs, emphasizing mitigation and next steps — draft by 2026-03-09.

Meeting notes excerpt (2026-03-03 installs sync):
Attendees: Priya, Evan, Lucas, Sophie, Diego, Kiran (SRE), Maya (Solutions)
- Kiran: "We need signals — today we only see application-level failures, not the PMTU life-cycle."
- Sophie: "Customer networking teams are wary of full-blown changes; provide minimal change checklist and a rollback plan."
- Decision: telemetry first, guided fix second; shim maintained until post-change verification.

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Can we ship a more robust shim that does MSS clamp + periodic controlled MTU probe that automatically adjusts, or does that cross the risk boundary for customer trust?
- What is our recommended support stance if a customer refuses to change network config and wants the shim permanently? (pricing? SLA carve-out?)
- Is there any vendor NIC firmware/version combination we've missed that systematically fails LSO/GSO with our workloads?

Communication plan:
- Customer-facing: Sophie to lead HelixAI and Pylon comms — provide timeline, clear rollback plan, and a simple explanation of why the shim is temporary.
- Internal: place this note in the private-deployments drive and link DEPLOY tickets to the install playbook change set.

Next-week goals (concrete):
- Complete telemetry prototype and circulate dashboard to SRE/Installs for feedback.
- Customer checklist finalized and validated with a single non-production test at Pylon Health.
- Decide on permanent solution spectrum: (A) telemetry + customer tweak, (B) packaged shim with automated probes, (C) formal support/SLA add-on if shim is to be permanent.

Attachments / artifacts to review (lab traces and links):
- tcpdump captures: s3://redwood-internal/mtu-traces/helixai-20260225.pcap (note: access via SRE account)
- DEPLOY tickets: DEPLOY-421 (telemetry), DEPLOY-430 (shim improvements)
- Design draft: confluence.redwood.ai/display/PD/MTU+Shim+Design

Notes to self / informal:
- Keep language simple when talking to networking teams — avoid kernel jargon on first pass.
- Track how long shim has been active per-customer; set calendar reminder for day-13 to force a re-check.
- There may be other customers silently protected by existing shims — run a quick query to see how many installs currently have MSS-clamp enabled by default.

If you need anything urgent on this, ping me on Slack (@priya) and put "MTU" in the subject.

--- end of journal entry ---
